bead.title: Persist emission cursor in sqlite backends: part 1
bead.description:
PROBLEM
Parent bead pqueue-615f2047 is too broad for one execution pass. This child owns part 1 of 2 of that parent scope.

ROOT CAUSE
PROBLEM: the sqlite family still has no durable change-record cursor, so a reopen cannot resume from the last emitted position and the engine falls back to the no-op default.
ROOT CAUSE: `crates/pqueue-engine/src/compose.rs:138-149` still supplies the default no-op cursor API; `crates/pqueue-sqlite/src/compose_log.rs:232-266` only persists `high_water`, and `crates/pqueue-sqlite/src/relational.rs:8356-8387` exposes only the relational high-water analogue. There is no sqlite reopen path that restores a durable emission cursor today.
PROPOSED FIX: add durable `emission_cursor` and `set_emission_cursor` storage for both sqlite log and sqlite relational backends, wire reopen to read that cursor before the first emit, and add file-backed reopen tests that emit, drop the backend, reopen the same store, and verify only the unacked tail re-emits.
NON-SCOPE: do not redo 42ef0f8's port-routed emit path, advance-after-sink-ack ordering, off-commit-path, opt-out filtering, or epoch-stable dedup key; do not change sqlite projection, leases, or recovery behavior outside the emission-cursor seam.

PROPOSED FIX
Implement only this child acceptance slice:
- `TestEmissionCursorPersistsAcrossReopen_SqliteLog`
- `TestEmissionCursorPersistsAcrossReopen_SqliteRelational`

NON-SCOPE
Do not implement parent acceptance criteria assigned to sibling child beads. Preserve every parent non-scope constraint unless this child explicitly narrows it.
